question.problem: A salesperson has a $72%$ chance of closing a sale on any given call. The salesperson continues making calls until they close a sale. Rounded to $3$ decimal places, the probability that they will make exactly $6$ calls is{{field-1}}.
question.worked_solution:
A geometric random variable $X$ with probability of success $p$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=(1-p)^{x-1}p
$$

Let $X$ be the number of calls made until the salesperson closes a sale. Since the chance of closing a sale is $72%,$ the number of calls until the salesperson closes a sale can be modeled as a geometric random variable with a probability of success

$$
p=72%=\frac{72}{100}=0.72.
$$

So, $X∼\text{Geom}(0.72).$ In this case, $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =(1-0.72)^{x-1}(0.72) \\  & =(0.28)^{x-1}(0.72)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the probability that the salesperson will close their first sale on the $6$th call is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X=6) & =f(6) \\  & =(0.28)^{6-1}(0.72) \\  & =(0.28)^{5}(0.72) \\  & ≈0.001,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
